bug_semantics: Composer Perforce::generateP4Command() built a single shell string by concatenating the p4 executable with unescaped -u (user), -c (client), and -p (port) values, then ProcessExecutor::execute() ran that string via the shell. A malicious root composer.json (or composer config) declaring a type=perforce VCS repository could put shell metacharacters in repositories[].url (copied to VcsDriver::$url and Perforce::$p4Port), repositories[].p4user, and the depot-derived client name. PerforceDriver::initialize() calls p4Login()/isLoggedIn()/connectClient(), so generateP4Command() runs during ordinary Composer use of that project. A payload such as url=localhost:1666; touch /tmp/pwned becomes `p4 -u … -p localhost:1666; touch /tmp/pwned …`; the shell still executes the injected command if p4 is missing. Dependency composer.json files are not a vector. Distinct from GHSA-gqw4-4w2p-838q (unescaped $sourceReference on sync) and from later rsh:/jsh: P4PORT transport execution.
flaw_origin: On 2013-07-25 matt-whittom first extracted Perforce::generateP4Command() in 36dd7dfea5b7c42adab172aa9985c0cd479aab42 and interpolated getUser()/getClient()/getPort() into a p4 command string with no quoting. Parent 0d061f25300062067488b64c35ff28d3cc0bedf8 ('Added Perforce to Composer') had no generateP4Command and did not interpolate port/user/client as -u/-c/-p. Subsequent style, typing, and partial-escape commits (including 3773f7752 escaping only the client-spec path) left those three fields raw until the 2026-04-14 GHSA patch.

BIC src/Composer/Util/Perforce.php lines 112-118: protected function generateP4Command($command) concatenates "p4 ", "-u ".$this->getUser(), "-c ".$this->getClient(), "-p ".$this->getPort(), and $command with no escape.

git grep generateP4Command 0d061f25300062067488b64c35ff28d3cc0bedf8 -- src/Composer/Util/Perforce.php: no matches. Parent file only interpolates $clientSpec/$p4client in syncCodeBase ("p4 client -i < $clientSpec", "p4 sync -f //$p4client/..."), not -u/-c/-p port/user/client.

64bda65e116d19cd97e8ddf2449d14b01ed727b8 only added $useClient to the already-vulnerable helper; not a first-write. Later refactors (71c8735e, 2223b93e, 6da38f83, 89ce5325, 3dc279cf) preserved unescaped concatenation.

2.9.5 src/Composer/Util/Perforce.php:308-317 still does $p4Command .= '-u '.$this->getUser() etc. executeCommand() at 150-154 passes the string to ProcessExecutor::execute(). isLoggedIn() (320-323) and connectClient() (340-345) call generateP4Command(); PerforceDriver::initialize() at 2.9.5:38-51 calls p4Login() then connectClient(). VcsDriver copies repoConfig['url'] to $this->url; Perforce::create($repoConfig, $this->getUrl(), ...) stores it as $p4Port; repoConfig['p4user'] and depot-derived client feed -u/-c.

reasoning: CVE-2026-40176 is a confirmed, unwithdrawn OS command injection in Composer’s Perforce helper: generateP4Command() interpolated attacker-controlled connection parameters into a shell string that ProcessExecutor ran even without a p4 binary. The smallest public first-write of those lines is 36dd7dfea5b7c42adab172aa9985c0cd479aab42 (2013-07-25), a single-parent non-merge whose parent tree lacks generateP4Command and lacks -u/-c/-p interpolation; git log -L later hits 64bda65e only as a $useClient refactor of the same helper, so that commit is not the BIC. No finer public members exist to decompose. Tag membership matches the advisory: BIC precedes 1.0.0/2.2.26/2.3.0/2.9.5; the GHSA squash 4f02616e6 (escape of user/client/port, with injection tests) lands in 2.9.6 and is mirrored on 2.2 LTS as d9ffd9c9 in 2.2.27.
